title: Office Inference client manifest
description: The single source of truth for what a client has turned on and where it runs.

agentic.description: The tasks this deployment can be asked to do. **This is what the client app's Do screen is built from**, and it lives in the manifest rather than in the API's source because the app is a function of the deployment: a client with no agentic pack has no tasks, and therefore no Do screen, which is the honest outcome rather than a menu of things that cannot run. A deployment that declares none behaves exactly as it did before this block existed.

tasks.description: Each entry is a thing a person can start. The API matches on `id` and routes on `tier`, so the label a client reads and the model that answers come from one declaration and cannot drift apart.

id.description: The identifier a request carries in its `task` field. Lowercase with underscores, because it is matched exactly and a space in it would be a task nobody can start.

label.description: The task in the client's words, shown as-is. 'Draft the recall texts' rather than 'draft'. This is the field that makes the Do screen readable to a person who has never seen the system.

description.description: One sentence about what it does, shown under the label.

tier.description: The model role that handles this task, as named in `models`. **This is what lets one task go to the cheap model and another to the frontier one without the interface choosing a model**: the app sends a task and the manifest decides which tier answers it.

touches.description: What the task reads or changes, in plain words, so the interface can say what it will touch before somebody starts it.

needs_approval.description: Whether a human has to approve before work happens. The approval gate itself arrives with the agentic pack; this is the declaration the interface renders.

access.description: What a user is told when a query is denied because content exists that their role may not see. The choice is the client's because the trade is theirs: disclosing reveals that restricted content EXISTS, and staying silent means an incomplete answer is indistinguishable from a complete one. Under a compliance profile this belongs in the contract, the same way the content modes do.

denial.description: silent: nothing is disclosed, and the answer is built from what the role can see. denied: the user is told that documents exist which may answer the question and that they lack access, with no count. counted: the same plus how many passages were withheld. The default is denied, because a silent system returns a partial answer that looks complete, which is the failure this product exists to avoid.

egress.description: What may leave for a frontier model. The gate refuses rather than defaulting, so a deployment that declares nothing sends nothing off-box, which is the office shape and the safe direction for a cloud one to fail in. Classes are the four the audit record already uses.

frontier_classes.description: Which data classes a client permits on a frontier lane. An empty list means nothing leaves, and it is the default because an unset permission must not become a permission. Listing regulated here is a client decision the system enforces and records rather than one it second-guesses.

redaction.description: Whether identifiers are replaced before a request leaves. On by default: the cost of redacting something harmless is a question the model cannot answer, and the cost of not redacting a card number is a payment incident in a provider's logs. Turning it off is a client's decision to make and one they should have to make explicitly.

roles.description: Optional. What each role may read, by role name. A role is what a session claims; a group is what a person belongs to, and a subject's permission is the union of the two. Declaring none gives the deployment one role named viewer that carries no roots of its own, which is the usual case when access is written with groups.

roots.description: Every access boundary this deployment uses, and the value written into a chunk's acl label. Declaring the full set here means a document labelled with a root no role and no group carries is reported rather than silently unreachable.

groups.description: Named unions of roots. A group is how a person's access changes over time: a job changes, a group changes, and no code moves. Access is a union with no deny rules and no precedence, which is what makes the model testable to exhaustion.

additionalProperties.description: The roots a group carries. **Two forms, and the mapping is the documented one.** The renderer accepts both, and the schema accepted only the bare list until this was found: the mapping form is what the manual shows and what every manifest in this repository uses, so every one of them was invalid against its own schema while the validator reported them all clean. A schema nobody enforces is documentation, and documentation that disagrees with the code is worse than none.

users.description: The subjects this deployment knows, and the groups each belongs to. A subject not declared here cannot hold a session once the deployment declares any users at all.

subject.description: The identifier the identity provider will assert at C7. An email address in every deployment so far.

name.description: For the manual's worked examples and the operator's read of the registry. Never used for a decision.

groups.description: At least one, because in a declared registry access comes from groups and a user without one resolves to nothing.

data_class.description: What a request on this deployment is, which is what the egress gate compares against access.egress.frontier_classes. The default is the most restrictive class, so a deployment that declares nothing does not send content to a remote lane by omission.

budgets.description: Per-role ceilings in USD over a period, enforced by the gateway, which refuses a request once recorded spend is over the ceiling. Internal cost control, not client billing. Required wherever the frontier lane is enabled, because a remote call costs money. NOT a hard cap, and the wording matters: LiteLLM checks admission against RECORDED spend, so concurrent requests can all pass before any of them is counted, and the global spend counter is known to lose concurrent increments (issues #34732 and #35567, open as of 2026-10-14). Treat this as a budget that stops a runaway, never as a number that cannot be exceeded. The enforced ceilings are the egress gate, which decides what may leave at all, and a per-request max_tokens.

roles.description: One amount per model role declared in this manifest.

content.description: What the record keeps per data class. Prompt and completion hashes are recorded whatever this says; only the text is governed here. Under a compliance profile this is a client decision that belongs in the contract, because 'full' means the record holds what was said.

models.description: One entry per role. A role is a name a caller asks for, mapped to a model, with its own key and ceiling, so a deployment may add its own. The three named in required are the ones every build needs; coder and anything else are additional.

offsite.description: Where audit artifacts go off this machine. Absent means nowhere, which is a valid office shape. An AWS account for this is not what makes a build hybrid: hybrid means both inference lanes. See docs/audit-evidence.md.

bucket.description: S3 bucket in the owner's account, created by Terraform at C7.

ship.description: An allowlist. Documents and prompts can never appear here.

packs.description: Pack ids from packs/catalog.yaml. The Core pack is implicit.

local.description: Model id served on the office box.

frontier.description: Model id used when the frontier lane is on.
